summary: Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1923–1928) and held posts at Breslau (~1936–1939), Halle-Wittenberg (~1939–1945), Frankfurt (~1953–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Breslau, and Halle-Wittenberg. His academic career included posts at Berlin (1918–1924), Frankfurt (1929–1933), Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (~1955–1962), and Chicago (~1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll, a sinologist and linguist, studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976). He held academic appointments at the University of Colorado Boulder, including associate professor and department chair (~1979) and faculty fellow (attested 2001).

Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sussex (~1969–1972) and Oxford (Wadham College, ~1972–1978). He served at Bristol (attested 1998–2016) and held a chair at Calgary (~2002).

Paula Kane Robinson Arai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at Kalamazoo College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith, later holding posts at Vanderbilt (~1994–2002) and LSU (~2007).

Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Yangon (~1904–1909) and the University of Calcutta (~1909–1911), later serving as Professor of Pali at the University of Yangon (~1912–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Wu studied at National Taiwan University and UCLA, completing a PhD under Donald F. McCallum, and was taught by Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Peipei Qiu is a scholar in Japanology and Sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where she was taught by Paul Rouzer, and held an academic post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

Pema Bhum is a Tibetology scholar. He served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and was director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who attended Miss Porter's School and the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Education. She studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa, Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and Sakyong Mipham.

Penghao Sun is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. Sun completed doctoral work under Leonard van der Kuijp, and studied under instructors including Qingying Chen, Mark C. Elliott, Peter K. Bol, Charles Hallisey, Jay Jasanoff, and Weirong Shen.
Pentti Aalto was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1949), where he later held an academic post (~1949–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen (~1972–1980), holding posts at Copenhagen (~1981–1994), Bonn (1991–1992), and Leipzig University (1995).

Per Kvaerne is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1964–1973), served there as professor (~1975–2007), and was Secretary General of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1989–1995).

Perry Link is a Sinology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harvard University (~1962–1976) and held faculty posts at Princeton University (~1989–2008) and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel is a religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic posts at Munich (~1988–1998), Innsbruck (~1996–1998), Salzburg (~1998–2000), Glasgow (~2000–2009), and Münster (~2009–2020).
Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctorate under supervisor Michael Aris.

Peter Bisschop is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden (attested 2011–2021).

Peter Connolly is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and held a post as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.
